gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the cables side by side in the same terms. Only BLUETTI states a current rating (20 A on its MC4-to-XT60 cable, 30 A on its MC4 extension). EcoFlow and Jackery give only length and connectors, with no amps or wire gauge. On EcoFlow's own US store, the XT60i cable that ChatGPT carded as '3.5m' is the 2.5 m (8.2 ft) version; the 3.5 m cable is the plain XT60 one.
standout_why: I compared four pages. yourpowersetup.com (cited) says XT60i differs from XT60 in 'communication and current behavior' but gives no numbers, no cable ratings and no gauges. stormwatts.com/solar-panel-compatibility (cited) lists each station's input current per port, for example DELTA 3 Plus 15 A, AC180 10 A and C1000 Gen 2 14.5 A, but says outright that it gives no cable amp ratings or gauges. powerstationtips.com (uncited, ranked 3) covers gauge and voltage drop and XT60 connector ratings, and contradicts itself on XT60 (30 A vs 60 A). It names no maker cable ratings and does not mention the 8 A cap. None of them sets the makers' cable specs against each other or catches that EcoFlow's XT60i cable comes in a different length from the XT60 one.
decides: For EcoFlow XT60i stations (DELTA 3 Plus, RIVER 3), the cable to buy is EcoFlow's Solar to XT60i cable, and it is 2.5 m, not 3.5 m. A plain MC4-to-XT60 lead, including EcoFlow's own 3.5 m XT60 version, fits the port but may not get the full port current. Solar Waypoint says plain XT60 leads can be held to 8 A or 10 A, but it has no test data and calls this rare. So if you need more reach, add an MC4 extension on the panel side rather than buying the longer cable. Of the maker cables I checked, only BLUETTI's states a current rating (20 A for $29), so it is the only one you can check against a port's limit from the spec sheet. For the generic 10 AWG MC4 extensions ChatGPT recommended, the gauge is the only number to compare. Jackery's DC8020 extensions (5 m / 10 m) state no rating at all.
